knowledge_gaps: The corrected baseline’s existing terminal-mask frequency is unspecified. A 0.5 example mixture does not imply 50% terminal supervision when reconstruction examples contain multiple targets; the actual change may be small or may substantially reduce supervised targets per update.

Endpoint sampling and loss normalization are undefined. Specify user versus interaction sampling, eligible endpoint distribution, reconstruction masking rate, treatment of repeated items, negative eligibility, and whether loss averages over targets or examples. These choices can confound the proposed objective-alignment experiment.

The comparison needs a fixed checkpoint-selection rule, baseline validation results, paired per-category uncertainty, and an explicit GPU-time allocation within the remaining shared budget. Fixed update counts alone do not equalize supervision or compute.

Disjoint diagnostic users are still training users whose interactions may have been fitted. Confirmation supports generalization of intervention effects across probe examples, not generalization to unseen training data or improved host validation.

The report redirects the residual-patching proposal toward training without measured evidence that objective mismatch causes the observed errors. Terminal masking is a reasonable comparator, but the claimed preference over the bounded patching pilot remains a judgment.

Originality 3 is reasonable. Potential 7 and difficulty 3 are provisional: benefit is unmeasured, and sampler changes also require diagnostic compatibility, deterministic random-number handling, and preservation of the B×L positive/negative loader contract.

The implementation checklist omits the required full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five training users per category. The conflicting generic metadata examples must also remain subordinate to the explicit restrictions on available fields.
